common_name: Andros Azalea (Double-Flowered Glenn Dale Hybrid, Sister to Delos)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade; Andros is a Glenn Dale hybrid grown for its unusually full, double flowers.

directions: Andros is a double-flowered Glenn Dale hybrid azalea raised by USDA breeder B.Y. Morrison, sharing its parentage with the related cultivar Delos out of the same cross. Its light purplish-pink blooms carry an extra whorl of petal-like stamens, giving a fuller, more layered look than the single flowers typical of most Glenn Dale introductions. The evergreen shrub keeps a rounded, medium habit and flowers in mid-to-late spring. Grow in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade, and limit pruning to right after flowering since next year's buds form soon afterward.

common_name: May Blaine Azalea (Back Acres Hybrid Satsuki Cross)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; May Blaine is a Back Acres hybrid bred for Gulf Coast heat and humidity.

directions: May Blaine is one of B.Y. Morrison's Back Acres hybrids, raised at his Pass Christian, Mississippi garden from a cross of the Satsuki cultivars Kagetsu and Warai Gishi. Flowering in late spring, it carries the richly saturated purplish-pink tones of its Warai Gishi parent on a compact, rounded evergreen shrub. Like other Back Acres selections, it tolerates more Gulf Coast heat and humidity than many older azalea lines. Grow in moist, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade, and prune only right after bloom since flower buds set soon afterward.
